full_judgment:
2. Material facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, briefly, are that Sekander Ali Sikder, the predecessor of the opposite party Nos.1-4 as plaintiff on 9-1-1990 instituted a suit being Title Suit No.5 of 1990 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Barguna for declaration of title in the land as described in Schedule "Ka" to the plaint alternatively for recovery of possession and partition of the land as described in Schedule "Kha" to the plaint. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that 16.35 acres of land appertaining to cadastral survey Khatian No. 205 of Mouza Kewrabunia belonged to Tamejuddin, Magezuddin in two annas share each and Ditio Bibi, Melancho Bibi, Sahera Bibi and Kanu Bibi in one ana share each; that the aforesaid holding was put to auction for arrear of rent and purchased by Nawab Estate who by a registered kabuliat dated 25-3-1912 settled the same with Kalu Sikder, Solemuddin, Asaruddin, Toberuddin, Ainuddin alias Sasanuddin, Amiruddin, Tamizuddin and Mafizuddin in equal share; that Asaruddin died leaving behind one son Montajuddin and one daughter JahuraBibi; that at the death of Salimuddin his interest devolved on his five sons named Kalu Sikder, Tasimuddin, Hasonuddin, Mahabbat Ali and Nasaruddin and two daughters named Kalsum and Serupannessa; that Kalu Sikder got two annas six gandas two Karas and two Karanties share, who died leaving behind only' son, the plaintiff, as his sole heir; that the land of candestral survey khatian No. 205 subsequently recorded in Revisional Settlement khatian No. 14 corresponding to state acquisition khatian Nos. 658,1048,1117,1150,1157 increasing to an area of 16.59 acres; that out of two ann as six gandas two karas and two kerantis share only two annas share had been recorded in the name of Kalu Sikder and rest six gandas two karas and two krantis share was wrongly recorded in the names of Mahabbat Ali and Nasaruddin; that plaintiffs total claim is 2.42 acres of land out of which 1.27 acres had been recorded in state acquisition Khatian No. 1117 and out of rest 1.15 acres 5 and 1/2 decimals had been recorded in the names of Mahabbat Ali and Nasaruddin in State Acquisition Khatian Nos. 117 and 16 and 1/2 decimals of land in state Acquisition Khatian No. 658 in the Dame of Tasanuddin Sikdar wrongly; that earlier the plaintiff filed a suit being title suit No. 189 of 1979 but for formal defects got it withdrawn with permission to sue afresh; that the defendants are the heirs and successive heirs of Hasanuddin, Mahabbat Ali, Nasaruddin, Tasanuddin, Montejuddin, Sonemuddin and Mufejuddin and some of the defendants are the purchasers from co-sharers of the suit jama; that there was no partition by metes and bounds in the suit jama, the defendants refused to partition the land amicably on 9-2-1979 and hence, the suit. 

 4. Defendant Nos. 1, 11, 12 in their written statement denied the all material allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner inasmuch as the suit is barred by limitation, all the relevant properties were not brought into hotchpotch; that Salemuddin Sikder took settlement of Ten ann as share in the suit lama from the Nawab Estate by a registered Kabuliat dated 25-3-1912; that the' said kobuliat contains the names of his four-sons, all of whom used to live in same mess; that Salemuddin had been in possession of Ten anas share in cadastral survey khatian No. 205; that Mahabbat Ali, son of Solernuddin by his second wife, on attaining to the age of majority went to live in separate mess with her mother; that Salemuddin Sikder within the knowledge of his other sons sold 1.08 acres of land to his son Mahabbat Ali by a kabala deed dated 22-4-1926; that Salemuddin Sikder made an oral gift of the rest along with other lands in favour of Kalu Sikder, Asaruddin, Habanuddin, Tasanuddin, Nasaruddin and Mahabbat Ali on 2nd Ashar, thirteen hundred thirty three Bengali Shal; that Saleinuddin died leaving behind 6(six) sons and two daughters as heirs; that in this manner Mahabbat Ali got two annas and ten gandas and his other brothers got one anna and ten gandas share that the property left by Asaruddin was inherited by his sons Montajuddin and Asahar Sikder and daughter lahure Bibi; that on 8-1-1947 Hersauddin, Mahabbat Ali, Kalu Sikder. Nasaruddin, Montajuddin settled 3.33 acres of land of cadastral survey Khatian No. 205 with Tasanuddin and on that date the kabuliat and dakhila were registered towards the recognition of tenant by the landlord; that Mahabbat Ali died leaving 3 sons, namely defendant Nos. 10-12 and two daughters namely, Chandra Banu and Suruj Banu; that Nasaruddin died leaving behind defendant Nos. 7 and 8; that Akub Ali died leaving defendant Nos. 4-6 as his legal heirs; that Kalu Sikdar after transfer of his one annas ten gandas share to Tasonuddin died leaving only 88 decimals of land but more than 88 decimals of land was recorded in the name of plaintiffs father; that by successive inheritance defendant No. 1 got the property of Tamijuddin; that defendant No. 63 transferred 99 decimals of land of State acquisition Khatian No. 1150 to defendant No. 12, Taiab Ali and others by six kabala deeds; that defendant No. 53 sold 43 decimals of land to Afam Ali by Kabala deed dated 18-2-1967; that Abdul Hoq heir of Adam Ali sold 7 and 1/2 decimals ofland to defendant No. 12 by kabala deed dated 16-6-1984; that after the death of Tasenuddin his wife Rupsan Bibi transferred 21 decimals from state acquisition Khatian No. 658 and 12 and 1/2 decimals of land from State Acquisition Khatian No. 1150 to defendant Nos. 1-4 by Kabala deed dated 24-4-1965; that defendant No. 32 and his brother Yousuf Ali transferred 17 decimals from State acquisition Khatian No. 1117 to defendant Nos. 2-4 and that the claim of the plaintiff is false and without any legal basis.
